title: One-Pot Turkey, Cabbage & Cheddar Rice
description: Ground turkey, cabbage, and rice cook together in one skillet, with cheddar stirred in at the end for an affordable comfort dinner.
substitutions: Use ground chicken instead of turkey.
Use bagged coleslaw mix instead of slicing cabbage.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Brown the turkey and soften the cabbage.
Simmer the rice in the same skillet and finish with cheese.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 pound ground turkey in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Cook 5–6 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until no pink remains.
Stir in 3 cups sliced cabbage and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder if using. Cook 3 minutes, until the cabbage starts to soften.
Stir in 1 cup white rice and 2 1/4 cups chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, cover, and reduce the heat to low.
Cook covered for 15–17 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from the heat, stir in 3/4 cup shredded cheddar, season to taste, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat until steaming hot, adding a splash of broth or water if the rice seems dry.

title: Egg, Spinach & Cheddar Toast Pockets
description: Soft scrambled egg, spinach, and cheddar tuck into toasted bread for a quick breakfast, lunch, or light dinner.
substitutions: Use frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry.
Use Monterey Jack or mozzarella instead of cheddar.
Use tortillas instead of toast and roll the filling into wraps.

steps.text: Toast the bread and scramble the eggs with spinach.
Fill the toast with egg and cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Toast 4 slices sandwich bread while you cook the eggs.
Beat 3 eggs. Heat 1 teaspoon butter or oil in a small skillet over medium-low heat, add 1 cup spinach, and cook about 1 minute until wilted.
Pour in the eggs and cook, stirring gently, for 2–3 minutes until softly set. Stir in 1/2 cup shredded cheddar and remove from the heat.
Divide the egg mixture between 2 slices of toast, top with the remaining toast, and serve warm.

storage: Best eaten right away. Refrigerate leftover egg filling up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot before assembling fresh toast.

title: Leftover Chicken, Corn & Noodle Bowls
description: Leftover cooked chicken and frozen corn turn instant-style noodles into a more complete quick meal without a special sauce.

ingredients.item: dry ramen noodles or thin wheat noodles

substitutions: Use leftover turkey instead of chicken.
Use frozen peas or mixed vegetables instead of corn.
Use spaghetti broken in half; allow extra cooking time as directed on the package.

steps.text: Simmer the noodles and corn in broth.
Warm the leftover chicken and season.

cookSteps.text: Bring 2 cups chicken broth to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Add 4 ounces noodles and 1 cup frozen corn.
Cook according to the noodle package, usually 3–5 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups shredded cooked chicken and 1 tablespoon soy sauce if using. Simmer 2–3 minutes, until the chicken is steaming hot.
Divide the noodles, chicken, corn, and broth between 2 bowls and serve.

storage: Use the chicken within its original safe refrigerated storage window. Refrigerate the finished noodles up to 3 days; the noodles will soften in the broth.

title: Small-Batch Peanut Butter Banana Pudding Cups
description: Banana, peanut butter, vanilla pudding, and crushed cookies make two easy chilled dessert cups with no baking.

ingredients.item: vanilla wafers or graham cracker squares, crushed

substitutions: Use chocolate pudding instead of vanilla.
Use sunflower-seed butter if peanut butter is not suitable.
Use crushed cereal instead of cookies for a less-sweet crunch.

steps.text: Layer with banana and cookie crumbs.

cookSteps.text: Stir 2 tablespoons peanut butter into 1 cup prepared vanilla pudding until mostly smooth.
Divide half of the pudding between 2 cups. Add half of 1 sliced banana and half of the crumbs from 4 cookies.
Repeat the layers with the remaining pudding, banana, and cookie crumbs.
Eat right away for crisp crumbs, or chill up to 30 minutes for a softer pudding-cup texture.

storage: Best the day it is made because banana darkens and cookie crumbs soften. Refrigerate covered and eat within 24 hours.
